findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] website_name reconstructs the display name as host + URI(...).path only, discarding the query string and fragment, so a same-domain website like 'http://example.com/topic/1?u=foo' displays as 'example.com/topic/1'. Users on same-domain instances see a link text that no longer matches the href they navigate to; bites anyone whose profile URL carries a query string (e.g. tracking params or filtered views).

[ADVISORY] When website_host equals discourse_host and the URL has an empty path with a trailing slash ('http://example.com/'), website_name returns 'example.com/' with a trailing slash, and returns 'example.com' (no slash) when the path is empty without slash, producing inconsistent display of the identical logical URL. Profile pages on same-domain instances render 'example.com/' for URLs users entered as 'example.com', a cosmetic-but-visible inconsistency right in the h3 header.

[ADVISORY] website_name returns nil when the stored website has no scheme (URI('www.example.com').host is nil, swallowed by the rescue modifier), while include_website_name returns true because website.present? holds, so the serializer emits an explicit website_name: null while the old client-side websiteName produced the same null via split — but the new code hides the link entirely for scheme-less websites that Discourse historically normalizes/stores. Any profile whose website value lacks a protocol loses the globe/link row in the user header after this change; bites users whose website was saved as 'www.example.com'.

[ADVISORY] The removed websiteName controller property is only replaced by model.website_name in templates/user/user.hbs, but the property had multiple consumers in the app (user card / other profile templates referencing websiteName on the user controller or a card serializer that does not expose website_name). Any other template still referencing websiteName (e.g., the user card view) renders an empty website name after this change, and the user-card serializer does not include website_name at all, so the same-feature view silently loses the display.

[ADVISORY] The new website_name tests cover host-only, same-domain, and instance-is-subdomain cases, but omit the sibling case where the website host is a subdomain of the instance apex and of unequal part count (e.g., website 'http://www.example.com' against current_hostname 'example.com', which falls into the else branch because lengths differ and the >2 check fails). The 'www.example.com == example.com' case returns only 'www.example.com' without the path, an untested behavioral gap; a regression or refactor of the branch conditions would ship undetected.

[ADVISORY] The domain comparison website_host == discourse_host is case-sensitive while URI(...).host preserves the website's original casing (e.g., a user entering 'http://Example.com/page' yields host 'Example.com'), and the else-branch comparison via ends_with?/split likewise never downcases. A user with a mixed-case website URL on the same domain as the instance gets the bare host shown instead of the full path, and the split-based subdomain comparison misfires for capitalized apex domains, silently dropping the feature the PR claims to deliver.

[ADVISORY] No spec in the diff exercises include_website_name, i.e., the negative case where website is blank — the spec file's surrounding contexts were updated only for the filled-website path. The include-guard (which prevents an explicit null website_name attribute from reaching clients and breaking the template's if) is unverified; a serializer refactor that drops the include_ method would emit a null key and leave the globe icon rendering path undefined for all users without a website.

[BUG] The elsif branch treats a website on a *different* subdomain of the same registrable domain as 'the same domain' and returns the full path, going beyond the PR's stated intent of 'website domain is same as instance domain'. An instance at forum.example.com with a user website at www.example.com/some/long/path renders the full path 'www.example.com/some/long/path' in the profile header even though the domains differ — the very case the old websiteName host-only display was designed for; the inline comment even mislabels this branch as 'www.example.com == forum.example.com', confirming the equality claim is false.

[ADVISORY] The subdomain-parent comparison embeds hand-rolled domain-logic (dot-splitting and suffix matching with `ends_with?('.' << website_host)`) that is not traceable to any stated requirement and duplicates intent in three parallel branches. Operators on hosts with multi-part public suffixes (e.g. example.co.uk) get wrong classifications: instance forums.example.co.uk, website example.co.uk has different split lengths so the elsif is skipped and `ends_with?` misfires for any site matching '.co.uk'; the next maintainer editing this serializer must reverse-engineer the intended domain-equality rule from three comment lines.

[ADVISORY] `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed up to three times per serialization on the user-card/user-profile hot path with no extraction to a local variable. Every user card and profile render now performs repeated URI parsing for the same string; a regression here (e.g. someone adding another branch) multiplies the parsing, and readers must re-verify each parse is on the same input.

[ADVISORY] The spec adds no test for the case where the website has no path but the domain matches (e.g. website 'http://example.com' with instance 'example.com'), even though the serializer then returns 'example.com' + empty-string path via string concatenation. A future refactor of the path concatenation (e.g. switching to File.join or stripping trailing content) silently changes the displayed name for path-less websites, and no spec in this diff catches it.

[ADVISORY] The same-domain comparison uses naive dot-count label arithmetic, so branch 2 treats any two hosts sharing the same parent labels as same-site, including different registrable domains under a multi-label TLD (website 'x.co.uk' on instance 'y.co.uk' passes because split('.')[1..-1] == 'co.uk' == 'co.uk'). Users on multi-label-TLD instances (.co.uk, .com.au) see the full URL path displayed for websites that belong to entirely unrelated registrants, because the code has no public-suffix knowledge; the author's counter-argument 'it only affects display text' is correct that it is not a security issue, but the feature's stated contract (same domain as instance) is enforced with the wrong domain-boundary definition, so the display claim is false for a whole class of TLDs.

[ADVISORY] URI(website.to_s).host is nil for any website value without a scheme (e.g. a profile storing 'example.com/user' instead of 'http://example.com/user'), so website_name serializes as nil and the profile UI ({{#if model.website_name}} in user.hbs) hides the website entirely even though model.website is present. Any user whose saved website lacks a scheme gets no website line at all on their profile instead of a hostname link; the specs added in this diff cover only 'http://'-prefixed values, so this branch has zero coverage and a regression here would be invisible to CI.

[ADVISORY] The same-domain display string is built as website_host + URI(website).path, silently dropping the query string and fragment, and appending a trailing '/' when the website URL has an empty path (URI('http://example.com').path == '/' yields 'example.com/'). Users linking to 'http://example.com/page?u=123' on a same-domain instance see 'example.com/page' (query lost from the visible text) and bare-domain links render as 'example.com/' rather than 'example.com'; the link href remains correct, but the displayed name misrepresents the destination for every URL whose distinguishing part is in the query string.

[ADVISORY] The host-extraction + same-domain logic is parsed from the raw website string via URI() three separate times per serialization (URI(website.to_s) appears on lines 137, 141, and 143) with no single parsed object, so the three parses can be given subtly different transformations in future edits. The next editor changing normalization (e.g. adding a downcase or scheme-prefix fix) must update three call sites; missing one yields a display name computed from a different parse than the comparison, and there is no test covering the www.example.com == forum.example.com branch that the comment on line 144 advertises.

[BUG] The sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com == forum.example.com) expands the accepted intent, which was only 'website domain is same as instance domain', to treat any attacker-chosen sibling subdomain as the instance's own domain. A user on forums.example.com who sets their profile website to http://evil.example.com/phish gets it rendered as 'evil.example.com/phish' in the same full-path trusted style intended only for same-site links, silently widening the feature's accepted scope without explicit sign-off.

[BUG] The common 'www.' website case violates the PR's stated intent: a website of http://www.example.com/user on an instance hosted at example.com falls into the else branch (lengths 3 vs 2 unequal), discourse_host.ends_with?('.www.example.com') is false, and only the host is returned. The exact scenario users most expect — website www.example.com/user on example.com — does not show the complete URL path, so the artifact does not deliver the objective in its title for the canonical www variant.

[BUG] `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` returns nil for any website value stored without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com/user'), so website_name is nil and the profile shows no website line at all, whereas the deleted client-side code split('/')[2] handled bare-host values. Any user whose stored website lacks http:// loses the website display entirely — a regression from the prior rendering behavior for that input class, hidden by the fact that all new specs use scheme-prefixed URLs.

[ADVISORY] `website_name` is listed in untrusted_attributes even though it is a purely computed serializer attribute derived from `website`, not a stored model field. Clients can submit `website_name` in update payloads; since nothing reads it as an input, this either fails validation or is silently dropped, but it advertises a writable surface that does not exist and will confuse the next maintainer of the update-params contract.

[ADVISORY] The same-origin/same-registrar comparison for website_name is a case-sensitive string comparison while website_host comes from URI parsing of a user-controlled URL, a normalization mismatch (URI#host preserves the case the user typed). A user whose website is stored as http://EXAMPLE.COM/private-topic/123 on an instance with hostname example.com gets website_name 'EXAMPLE.COM' instead of the full path — purely a display inconsistency, and the reverse (attacker deliberately matching) only controls their own display text, since the href is model.website either way and Handlebars escapes the rendered value; report is advisory because no injection or privilege boundary is crossed.

[ADVISORY] The elsif branch of UserSerializer#website_name (lines where website_host and discourse_host have the same >2 part count) is completely untested — neither its true nor false case is exercised by any spec in this diff. A regression in the subdomain-equality comparison (e.g., www.example.com vs forum.example.com returning the host+path when it should return host only, or vice versa) would pass the entire suite; users with same-part-count sibling subdomains get wrong display paths. Checked spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb — its three cases hit the equal-host branch, and the else branch (length-mismatch/parent-domain), but never the same-length->3-parts elsif. A case like website='http://www.example.com/user', current_hostname='forum.example.com' (both 3 parts, matching parent → 'www.example.com/user') and website='http://forum.other.com', current_hostname='forum.example.com' (both 3 parts, mismatching parent → 'forum.other.com') would cover it.

[ADVISORY] No spec covers the rescue-nil/URI-parse-failure path of website_name, where website is present but malformed so website_name returns nil while include_website_name? returns true. The frontend template gates on {{#if model.website_name}}, so the website silently disappears from the profile for malformed URLs with no test pinning that behavior; a future change that makes website_name fall back to the raw string would silently alter profiles for invalid URLs with no failing spec. Checked spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb — no case sets a website that URI() cannot parse.

[BUG] `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` raises NoMethodError because Ruby's String only defines `end_with?`, not `ends_with?` (removed in Rails 3.1 and not present in Ruby core). For any site whose hostname has a different label count than the website host (e.g. forums.example.com hosting a profile with website example.com — the exact case this branch exists for), rendering the user serializer raises NoMethodError and the user profile/card request 500s.

[ADVISORY] The conditional-include hook is defined as `include_website_name` but ActiveModel::Serializers dispatches `include_website_name?` (with question mark), so this method is never invoked. The guard silently never runs; today the website_name method itself returns nil for missing websites so no user-visible bug results, but the next developer copying this pattern to gate an attribute without a nil-safe fallback will ship an attribute that is always included.

[ADVISORY] `website_name` is added to the untrusted-attributes list and is derived via `URI(website.to_s).host`, which for the same-domain branch re-appends `URI(...).path`; for URLs whose host matches but whose serialization came from `website` (raw user input), a path with a query string or fragment is silently truncated to just the path, dropping the query. A user on forums.example.com whose website is `http://example.com/t?u=alice` gets a displayed website_name of `example.com/t`, losing the query component — a silent fidelity loss between the stored URL and the displayed complete path.

[ADVISORY] The old client-side `websiteName` property (removed from user.js.es6) parsed `website.split("/")[2]`, while the new server-side logic compares against `Discourse.current_hostname`; any other in-tree consumer of the removed controller property that was not updated in this diff (e.g. user card / summary templates still referencing `websiteName`) will now render undefined instead of the domain. Any template or plugin still binding `websiteName` renders an empty link title after deploy; a grep of templates is needed since this diff only updates user.hbs.

[BUG] `rescue nil` swallows URI parse failures, so a website stored without a scheme (e.g. "example.com/user") serializes `website_name` as nil while `include_website_name` still returns true because `website.present?`, and the template's `{{#if model.website_name}}` then silently renders nothing. A user whose profile website is saved as a scheme-less or otherwise unparseable URI has their website link and globe icon silently disappear from their profile even though `website` is set and serialized — no error, no display, and no way to see why; the old JS `website.split("/")[2]` path did not have this all-or-nothing swallow for every parse error.

[ADVISORY] The new `website_name` logic has no spec covering the scheme-less/malformed-website path that hits the `rescue nil`. A regression in the nil-branch (e.g. someone later "fixes" the rescue to raise, 500ing every user serializer that touches a profile with an unparseable website) ships undetected, because the only exercised inputs are well-formed http URLs.

[ADVISORY] The same-domain detection (`split('.').length` equality and `ends_with?`) mis-handles multi-part public suffixes and case: a website host of "Forum.Example.Com" or a site on "example.co.uk" versus a hostname like "forum.example.co.uk" (length==3, matches the `> 2` branch only when lengths are equal, otherwise falls to the `ends_with?` branch) produces inconsistent path-vs-host display decisions. Users on instances with two-level TLDs get the truncated host shown (or the full path shown for a genuinely foreign site sharing the suffix), a display-logic divergence that will surface as scattered "my profile shows the wrong website text" reports; there is no log or signal distinguishing which branch decided.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

This is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/incompleteness in the new display-name logic, but it doesn’t break navigation (the `href` is unchanged), so it’s better characterized as a non-bug review concern rather than a definite defect.

Profile pages on same-domain instances render 'example.com/' for URLs users entered as 'example.com', a cosmetic-but-visible inconsistency right in the h3 header.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, when `website_host == discourse_host` it returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. Ruby `URI(...).path` is `"/"` for URLs like `http://example.com/` but `""` for `http://example.com`, so the serializer will return `"example.com/"` vs `"example.com"` for logically equivalent inputs. Since the template now renders `{{model.website_name}}` in the profile header (`user.hbs`), this inconsistency is user-visible and grounded in the new code path.

adjudication.rationale: In the new serializer method `website_name`, `URI(website.to_s).host` will be `nil` for scheme-less values like `"www.example.com"` and that `nil` is silently returned due to `rescue nil`. At the same time `include_website_name` returns true whenever `website.present?`, so the JSON can include `website_name: null`. This is a concrete edge case in the newly added server-side logic, but the claimed UI regression (“previously showed, now hides”) is not verifiable from the diff because the old client-side `websiteName` also returned `nil` for scheme-less inputs via `split('/')[2]`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `websiteName` being removed from `controllers/user.js.es6` and the *user profile* template (`templates/user/user.hbs`) being updated to use `model.website_name`, with `website_name` added to `UserSerializer`. However, the finding asserts breakage in other consumers (e.g., user card templates / a user-card serializer not exposing `website_name`). Those other templates/serializers are not present in the provided diff, so the claim about them rendering empty or missing `website_name` is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` (new `else` branch using `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host) ? website_host + URI(...).path : website_host`). The accompanying specs cover: different domain (`discourse.org`), same domain (`example.com`), and instance as subdomain of website (`forums.example.com`). They do not cover the case where `website_host` is a subdomain of the instance apex with unequal dot-part counts (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `example.com`), which would hit the `else` branch and currently return only `website_host` (dropping the path). That is a specific, diff-grounded missing edge-case test for newly added logic, not a proven functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on the claim that `URI(website.to_s).host` preserves the original casing and thus makes `website_host == discourse_host`/`ends_with?`/`split` comparisons misbehave for mixed-case input. From the diff alone, there’s no evidence that `URI(...).host` retains casing (Ruby’s URI parsing typically normalizes hostnames to lowercase), nor that `Discourse.current_hostname` could be mixed-case. Therefore the asserted case-sensitivity bug is not verifiable from the shown changes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `website_name` plus an include-guard `include_website_name` in `user_serializer.rb`, but the updated spec only covers the "with filled out website" context and asserts positive `json[:website_name]` values. There is no spec asserting the negative case (website blank) where `include_website_name` should prevent emitting the key. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded test gap for newly added conditional serialization logic (even if the template likely treats `null` as falsy).

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` intentionally treats same-length sibling subdomains as “same base domain” and returns `website_host + path` when `website_host.split('.')[1..]` equals `discourse_host.split('.')[1..]` (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`). However, the finding correctly identifies a potentially problematic/UX-regressive behavior and a misleading comment, grounded in that `elsif` branch.

This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/brittleness concern (nontrivial, hand-rolled host rules with limited tests). This is a real, diff-grounded performance/maintainability concern (re-parsing the same string repeatedly) but not a correctness defect.

The added specs only cover a website with a non-empty path (`http://example.com/user`) for the “same domain” case, plus two other hostname relationships, but do not cover the “same domain, no path” input (`http://example.com`). For a scheme-less website string, Ruby's `URI("example.com/user").host` is `nil`, so `website_name` would serialize as `nil` even though `include_website_name` would include it whenever `website.present?`. The UI was changed to gate display on `{{#if model.website_name}}`, so this edge case would cause the website line to disappear despite `model.website` being present. The added specs only cover `http://`-prefixed values and don't exercise this new parsing edge case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The same-domain display string is built as website_host + URI(website).path, silently dropping the query string and fragment, and appending a trailing '/' when the website URL has an empty path (URI('http://example.com').path == '/' yields 'example.com/'). Users linking to 'http://example.com/page?u=123' on a same-domain instance see 'example.com/page' (query lost from the visible text) and bare-domain links render as 'example.com/' rather than 'example.com'; the link href remains correct, but the displayed name misrepresents the destination for every URL whose distinguishing part is in the query string.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the display string is constructed with `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` in multiple branches. `URI(...).path` excludes the query string and fragment, so a URL like `http://example.com/page?u=123` would display as `example.com/page` (query dropped) even though the `href` remains `model.website`. Also, for a bare domain `URI('http://example.com').path` is `"/"`, so the displayed name becomes `example.com/`. This behavior is directly implied by the diff and can misrepresent the visible destination text.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The host-extraction + same-domain logic is parsed from the raw website string via URI() three separate times per serialization (URI(website.to_s) appears on lines 137, 141, and 143) with no single parsed object, so the three parses can be given subtly different transformations in future edits. The next editor changing normalization (e.g. adding a downcase or scheme-prefix fix) must update three call sites; missing one yields a display name computed from a different parse than the comparison, and there is no test covering the www.example.com == forum.example.com branch that the comment on line 144 advertises.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the code parses `URI(website.to_s)` multiple times (`URI(...).host` and `URI(...).path` in more than one branch). While not a correctness bug today, this duplicates parsing/normalization points and could lead to inconsistent behavior if future edits change normalization in only one place. Also, the spec additions cover three cases (different domain, same domain, parent-domain) but do not exercise the `elsif` branch intended for same-length subdomains (commented `# www.example.com == forum.example.com`), so that newly added nontrivial branch is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com == forum.example.com) expands the accepted intent, which was only 'website domain is same as instance domain', to treat any attacker-chosen sibling subdomain as the instance's own domain. A user on forums.example.com who sets their profile website to http://evil.example.com/phish gets it rendered as 'evil.example.com/phish' in the same full-path trusted style intended only for same-site links, silently widening the feature's accepted scope without explicit sign-off.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the sibling-subdomain branch `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` treats any host sharing the same parent domain (by comparing `split('.')[1..-1]`) as “equivalent” and returns `website_host + URI(...).path`. With `discourse_host = forums.example.com` and `website_host = evil.example.com`, it will return `evil.example.com/phish` (full path) rather than just `evil.example.com`. This does broaden when the “full-path” display format is used beyond the exact same host, but it does not change the actual link target (`href={{model.website}}`), and the displayed domain remains `evil.example.com`, so the finding’s implied security impact is not clearly a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The common 'www.' website case violates the PR's stated intent: a website of http://www.example.com/user on an instance hosted at example.com falls into the else branch (lengths 3 vs 2 unequal), discourse_host.ends_with?('.www.example.com') is false, and only the host is returned. The exact scenario users most expect — website www.example.com/user on example.com — does not show the complete URL path, so the artifact does not deliver the objective in its title for the canonical www variant.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the path is only appended when `website_host == discourse_host`, when both hosts have the same dot-segment length > 2 and share a parent, or when `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` (i.e., discourse host is a subdomain of the website host). For the common case `website_host = "www.example.com"` and `discourse_host = "example.com"`, none of those conditions match (lengths 3 vs 2; `ends_with?(".www.example.com")` is false), so the method returns only `website_host` (dropping `/user`). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral gap, and there is no test covering it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` returns nil for any website value stored without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com/user'), so website_name is nil and the profile shows no website line at all, whereas the deleted client-side code split('/')[2] handled bare-host values. Any user whose stored website lacks http:// loses the website display entirely — a regression from the prior rendering behavior for that input class, hidden by the fact that all new specs use scheme-prefixed URLs.

adjudication.rationale: The old client-side `websiteName` computed property (`website.split("/")[2]`) did not handle schemeless values like `example.com/user` either: splitting yields `["example.com","user"]` so index 2 is `nil`, and the template gated rendering on `{{#if websiteName}}`, so the website line would also not render previously. The new server-side `website_name` using `URI(...).host` likewise returns `nil` for schemeless URLs, but this is not a regression from behavior shown in the removed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `website_name` is listed in untrusted_attributes even though it is a purely computed serializer attribute derived from `website`, not a stored model field. Clients can submit `website_name` in update payloads; since nothing reads it as an input, this either fails validation or is silently dropped, but it advertises a writable surface that does not exist and will confuse the next maintainer of the update-params contract.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `website_name` is a computed serializer method derived from `website` and is added to `untrusted_attributes` (user_serializer.rb). However, nothing in the diff establishes that `untrusted_attributes` controls permitted/writable update params or that clients can submit `website_name` in update payloads because of this list. From the diff alone, this looks like an output/serialization concern, and the claimed “advertises a writable surface” behavior is not verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The same-origin/same-registrar comparison for website_name is a case-sensitive string comparison while website_host comes from URI parsing of a user-controlled URL, a normalization mismatch (URI#host preserves the case the user typed). A user whose website is stored as http://EXAMPLE.COM/private-topic/123 on an instance with hostname example.com gets website_name 'EXAMPLE.COM' instead of the full path — purely a display inconsistency, and the reverse (attacker deliberately matching) only controls their own display text, since the href is model.website either way and Handlebars escapes the rendered value; report is advisory because no injection or privilege boundary is crossed.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the branching relies on direct string comparisons like `website_host == discourse_host` and `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` without any normalization (e.g., downcasing). Since `website_host` is derived from `URI(website.to_s).host` on user-provided input, case differences can cause the "same domain" / "parent domain" logic to take the wrong branch and return just `website_host` instead of `website_host + path`, creating a real display inconsistency relative to the intent shown by the tests (which assume domain matching yields host+path).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The elsif branch of UserSerializer#website_name (lines where website_host and discourse_host have the same >2 part count) is completely untested — neither its true nor false case is exercised by any spec in this diff. A regression in the subdomain-equality comparison (e.g., www.example.com vs forum.example.com returning the host+path when it should return host only, or vice versa) would pass the entire suite; users with same-part-count sibling subdomains get wrong display paths. Checked spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb — its three cases hit the equal-host branch, and the else branch (length-mismatch/parent-domain), but never the same-length->3-parts elsif. A case like website='http://www.example.com/user', current_hostname='forum.example.com' (both 3 parts, matching parent → 'www.example.com/user') and website='http://forum.other.com', current_hostname='forum.example.com' (both 3 parts, mismatching parent → 'forum.other.com') would cover it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name`, including an `elsif` that triggers only when `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and that length is `> 2` (the sibling-subdomain case). The added specs cover (1) different 2-part domains (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`) hitting the final `else`, (2) exact host equality (`example.com` vs `example.com`) hitting the first `if`, and (3) parent-domain relationship with length mismatch (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`) also hitting the final `else`. No test sets both hosts to the same >2-part length (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), so the finding that this `elsif` branch is untested is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No spec covers the rescue-nil/URI-parse-failure path of website_name, where website is present but malformed so website_name returns nil while include_website_name? returns true. The frontend template gates on {{#if model.website_name}}, so the website silently disappears from the profile for malformed URLs with no test pinning that behavior; a future change that makes website_name fall back to the raw string would silently alter profiles for invalid URLs with no failing spec. Checked spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb — no case sets a website that URI() cannot parse.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds `website_name` in `UserSerializer` with `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and `include_website_name` returning `website.present?`. If `website` is present but unparsable, `website_name` returns `nil` while the attribute is still included, and the new template now gates display on `{{#if model.website_name}}` (so the website UI disappears). The updated spec only covers valid URLs (`http://example.com/user`) and does not exercise the rescue/parse-failure path, so this edge behavior isn’t pinned by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` raises NoMethodError because Ruby's String only defines `end_with?`, not `ends_with?` (removed in Rails 3.1 and not present in Ruby core). For any site whose hostname has a different label count than the website host (e.g. forums.example.com hosting a profile with website example.com — the exact case this branch exists for), rendering the user serializer raises NoMethodError and the user profile/card request 500s.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` in `UserSerializer#website_name`. In a Rails app, `String#ends_with?` is commonly provided by ActiveSupport (alongside `starts_with?`), so it is not verifiable from the diff alone that this will raise `NoMethodError`. The finding asserts a definite runtime failure based on Ruby core only, but the surrounding context is a Rails serializer where ActiveSupport extensions are typically loaded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The conditional-include hook is defined as `include_website_name` but ActiveModel::Serializers dispatches `include_website_name?` (with question mark), so this method is never invoked. The guard silently never runs; today the website_name method itself returns nil for missing websites so no user-visible bug results, but the next developer copying this pattern to gate an attribute without a nil-safe fallback will ship an attribute that is always included.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a new guard method named `include_website_name` (without a `?`), but it does not provide any evidence about how Discourse’s serializer framework dispatches conditional include hooks (e.g., whether it expects `include_website_name?` vs `include_website_name`). Without seeing the serializer base class or existing include-guard naming patterns in this codebase, the claim that the method is “never invoked” cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `website_name` is added to the untrusted-attributes list and is derived via `URI(website.to_s).host`, which for the same-domain branch re-appends `URI(...).path`; for URLs whose host matches but whose serialization came from `website` (raw user input), a path with a query string or fragment is silently truncated to just the path, dropping the query. A user on forums.example.com whose website is `http://example.com/t?u=alice` gets a displayed website_name of `example.com/t`, losing the query component — a silent fidelity loss between the stored URL and the displayed complete path.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the “same-domain” and related branches build the display string as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. `URI(...).path` omits the query string and fragment, so a stored URL like `http://example.com/t?u=alice#x` would display as `example.com/t`, silently dropping `?u=alice#x`. The spec calls this “complete website path” but doesn’t cover query/fragment, and the truncation is directly implied by using `.path` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The old client-side `websiteName` property (removed from user.js.es6) parsed `website.split("/")[2]`, while the new server-side logic compares against `Discourse.current_hostname`; any other in-tree consumer of the removed controller property that was not updated in this diff (e.g. user card / summary templates still referencing `websiteName`) will now render undefined instead of the domain. Any template or plugin still binding `websiteName` renders an empty link title after deploy; a grep of templates is needed since this diff only updates user.hbs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `websiteName` computed property from `controllers/user.js.es6` and only updates `templates/user/user.hbs` to use `model.website_name`. If any other in-repo template/component still references `websiteName`, it would now be undefined, but the diff doesn’t show whether such references exist, so the concern is about a potentially incomplete migration rather than a confirmed break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `rescue nil` swallows URI parse failures, so a website stored without a scheme (e.g. "example.com/user") serializes `website_name` as nil while `include_website_name` still returns true because `website.present?`, and the template's `{{#if model.website_name}}` then silently renders nothing. A user whose profile website is saved as a scheme-less or otherwise unparseable URI has their website link and globe icon silently disappear from their profile even though `website` is set and serialized — no error, no display, and no way to see why; the old JS `website.split("/")[2]` path did not have this all-or-nothing swallow for every parse error.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` will yield `nil` for scheme-less or otherwise non-host URIs (e.g. `"example.com/user"` parses with `host == nil`, or invalid URIs raise and are rescued). The method then `return if website_host.nil?`, so `website_name` becomes `nil` even though `website` is present. However `include_website_name` returns `website.present?`, so the serializer will still include a `website_name` attribute that can be `nil`, and the template now gates rendering on `{{#if model.website_name}}`, causing the website/globe to disappear while `model.website` still exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new `website_name` logic has no spec covering the scheme-less/malformed-website path that hits the `rescue nil`. A regression in the nil-branch (e.g. someone later "fixes" the rescue to raise, 500ing every user serializer that touches a profile with an unparseable website) ships undetected, because the only exercised inputs are well-formed http URLs.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds `UserSerializer#website_name` using `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and returns early when `website_host.nil?`, but the new specs only exercise well-formed `http://example.com/user` URLs and never hit the rescue/nil branch. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for newly added nontrivial parsing/branching logic, not an actual defect in the current implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The same-domain detection (`split('.').length` equality and `ends_with?`) mis-handles multi-part public suffixes and case: a website host of "Forum.Example.Com" or a site on "example.co.uk" versus a hostname like "forum.example.co.uk" (length==3, matches the `> 2` branch only when lengths are equal, otherwise falls to the `ends_with?` branch) produces inconsistent path-vs-host display decisions. Users on instances with two-level TLDs get the truncated host shown (or the full path shown for a genuinely foreign site sharing the suffix), a display-logic divergence that will surface as scattered "my profile shows the wrong website text" reports; there is no log or signal distinguishing which branch decided.

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` uses ad-hoc hostname comparisons (`split('.').length` equality and `ends_with?`) and does not normalize case before comparing `website_host` vs `Discourse.current_hostname`. While the diff doesn’t prove a concrete failing case, this kind of heuristic (especially `split`-count–based branching) is plausibly brittle for multi-part suffixes and differing host casing, and the added specs only cover simple `.com` scenarios (no coverage for `*.co.uk`/case variants). This is a diff-grounded robustness concern rather than a verifiable defect from the provided changes alone.
